block43_projection.teacher: Pinned pretrained reconstruction; not exact native intermediate features.
block43_projection.fit: Float64 centered ridge regression with an unpenalized intercept; ridge is fraction of mean covariance diagonal.
block43_projection.inference: FP16 matmul, FP16 bias add, E4M3 publication back to FP16.
limitations: Training and validation are first-reset camera views from one scene, with overlapping scene content.
Validation cameras guided the prior block-selection diagnostic and are not an independent final quality test.
The unmodified reconstruction already differs from native output.
Isolated block CUDA Graph timings exclude the surrounding model and application; not native speedup.
No weights, raw activations or captured images are published.

findings: Block 43 has the smallest worst-view final RGB change among the 59 supported same-shape removals.
No individual removal improves native RGB MAE on both diagnostic views; both group removals degrade the images.
A four-view affine feature projection improves agreement with the reconstructed teacher relative to deleting block43.
The projection still worsens native RGB MAE compared with the unchanged reconstruction on both views.
The isolated projection is about 9.2 times faster than the reconstructed block, not the native block or complete renderer.
limitations: The recovered model remains numerically different from NVIDIA before compression; its feature targets are not native truth.
These first-reset, same-scene camera diagnostics do not cover independent scenes, temporal stability, disocclusion or UI quality.
The two evaluation views informed block selection and are not an independent final test set.
Historical instrumented native intervals cannot be subtracted from later uninstrumented timings as guaranteed savings.
Native chained launch removal is not implemented or authorized by the cost map; synchronization and layouts must be retained.
No compressed model is installed. Only source, scalar results and hashes are published.
